FULL EXPERIMENT DESIGN (design-only; kuch bhi execute nahi kiya gaya, koi outcome claim nahi)

TITLE: ZB-2p automatic scheduling ka measured bubble rate — near-zero hai ya nahi, multi-GPU profiling par.

RESEARCH QUESTION (as given): Does the automatic scheduling algorithm's output (ZB-2p) truly achieve a near-zero bubble rate in practice when profiled on multiple GPUs?

EXPLICIT SCOPE STATEMENT: The empirical answer (near-zero vs not) remains OPEN. This design only operationalizes how it would be measured; no result is claimed.

=====================================================================
0) SOURCE / SETUP BASIS (assumptions, verification-first)
=====================================================================
- ASSUMPTION: Implementation = Megatron-LM fork "sail/zero-bubble-pipeline-parallelism" (official code of "Zero Bubble Pipeline Parallelism", Qi et al., 2024), which contains the zero-bubble scheduler and automatic scheduler (vsched-style timeline generator). The current sandbox has no repo/network, so at execution time step 0 is: clone the repo, and verify (i) exact flag names — `--enable-zero-bubble`, `--zero-bubble-max-pending-backward`, (ii) the automatic scheduler's entry point and output format (timeline dump / claimed bubble rate). If any flag name differs, use the source's actual name; the *semantic* activation (max pending backward = 2×p) is fixed by the task.
- ASSUMPTION: Execution happens on a separate multi-GPU machine (≥4, ideally 8× datacenter GPUs, e.g., A100/V100), CUDA + NCCL available, network available for cloning. The current sandbox (no GPU, no network) is design-only.
- ASSUMPTION: Single-node multi-GPU (NVMe/NVLink or PCIe) — this matches the paper's strongest zero-bubble claims and avoids cross-node variables.

=====================================================================
1) CONFIGURATION MATRIX
=====================================================================
Model: small GPT-style transformer chosen so scheduling dominates, not compute:
- hidden_size 1024, 8 layers, seq_len 512, vocab ~50k, TP=1, DP=1 (pipeline-only parallelism — bubble measurement needs PP to be the only parallelism dimension so every stage is a full-time worker).
- Rationale: with per-stage step time ~100-200 ms and micro-batches of 32-64, comm overhead per boundary is small relative to compute; if model were too big, all schedules would look compute-bound; too small → launch overhead dominates. If per-stage time <50 ms in practice, scale seq_len up once (tuning pass, reported separately).

Matrix (all arms × all cells):
| Cell | pipeline stages p | micro-batches m | GPUs used |
| A1 | 4 | 32 | 4 |
| A2 | 4 | 64 | 4 |
| B1 | 8 | 32 | 8 |
| B2 | 8 | 64 | 8 |
- TP=1, DP=1, world_size = p. Global batch = m (one micro-batch per pipeline "column" per iteration).
- ~20 warmup iterations + ~30-50 measured iterations per arm-cell (few enough to stay trivially within any budget; large enough for steady state).
- Rationale for m≫p: ZB-2p's zero-bubble claim is a steady-state property; small m would keep warmup/cooldown bubbles dominant and make "near-zero" unmeasurable.

=====================================================================
2) SCHEDULE ARMS & EXACT ZB-2p ACTIVATION
=====================================================================
All arms run on identical hardware, software, model, batch size, precision (bf16), and iteration count. Only the schedule flag differs:

- ARM 1 (baseline / positive control): 1F1B — default Megatron pipeline schedule (no zero-bubble flags).
- ARM 2: ZB-V — `--enable-zero-bubble` with default/symmetric pending (per fork semantics; verify at step 0).
- ARM 3 (treatment): ZB-2p — `--enable-zero-bubble` (or the fork's equivalent master flag, verified in step 0) PLUS `--zero-bubble-max-pending-backward 2p`:
  - Cell A (p=4): `--zero-bubble-max-pending-backward 8`
  - Cell B (p=8): `--zero-bubble-max-pending-backward 16`
  This matches the task's specified activation: flag enabled, value = twice the number of pipeline stages.
- ARM 4 (optional reference, only if it exists in the verified source and budget allows): ZB-H. Droppable without affecting the core answer; marked OPTIONAL.

Positive control logic: 1F1B's theoretical steady-state bubble fraction is (p−1)/(m+p−1). E.g., p=4, m=64 → 3/67 ≈ 4.5%; p=8, m=32 → 7/39 ≈ 17.9%. If measured 1F1B does not land within a reasonable tolerance (e.g., ±3 percentage points) of theory, the measurement pipeline is suspect and all results from that cell are quarantined.

=====================================================================
3) MEASUREMENT SPECIFICATION
=====================================================================
3.1 Per-stage timing capture:
- Per rank (pipeline stage) per micro-batch, record wall-clock timestamps of: forward start/end, backward start/end (both B segments if the fork splits them), and any explicit send/recv wait time the fork logs. Implementation: a thin instrumentation hook (timer wrapper around Megatron's schedule loop) writing a JSONL event log per rank: {rank, iter, mb, phase, t_start_ns, t_end_ns}. This is the primary timeline source and does not depend on the automatic scheduler's internal output.
- ALSO capture the automatic scheduler's own reported bubble rate (whatever it prints/outputs) — this is the "scheduler's claimed bubble rate" used in analysis §4.
- Memory per rank: torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated / reserved, logged per iteration (see §5 OOM control).

3.2 Steady-state window (warmup/cooldown exclusion):
- Timeline-based: for each measured iteration i and stage r, compute the interval [start_i, end_i] as: start = timestamp of the LAST rank beginning its first forward of iteration i (after warmup), end = timestamp of the FIRST rank completing its last backward. Steady-state window = measured iterations, with per-iteration boundaries taken from the pipeline's critical path; warmup iterations (first 20) and the trailing drain of the final iteration are excluded by computing bubbles only within [first steady start, last steady end] and normalizing per-iteration. Concretely: per-iteration bubble_b = Σ_r (idle time of rank r within the iteration window), bubble_rate_timeline = Σ_r bubble_r / (p × window_duration). Ranks idle during natural pipeline fill/drain at the very first/last micro-batch are excluded by the window construction; the residual per-iteration steady-state idle is what we measure.
- Robustness check: also report the version WITHOUT warmup/cooldown exclusion (full-window rate) — the difference quantifies how much of the schedule's apparent cost is transient.

3.3 Bubble-rate formulas:
- Method A (timeline-based): bubble_rate_A = (Σ_r Σ_iter idle_r,iter) / (p × total_steady_state_duration). idle_r,iter = window duration − (sum of compute-busy intervals of rank r in that window). Comm-wait and launch gaps count as busy-vs-idle only via the explicit categories in §4.
- Method B (throughput-based): ideal_time = Σ_r (F_time_r + B_time_r) × m (measured pure-compute micro-batch times, obtained from isolated single-stage microbenchmarks with comm disabled per stage, summed over ranks — i.e., the time if all stages were perfectly packed); bubble_rate_B = 1 − (ideal_time / measured_steady_state_time). Cross-check note: B is sensitive to comm overhead by construction, so A vs B disagreement is itself a finding (it localizes overhead to comm/launch rather than schedule structure).
- Theoretical reference: 1F1B steady-state bubble fraction = (p−1)/(m+p−1); ZB-2p (paper claim) = 0 (steady state, ignoring comm/launch).

3.4 Profiler cross-check:
- One run per arm-cell (subset: A1 and B2 at minimum) under torch profiler (activity CUDA+CPU, schedule wait=1/warmup=3/active=10) and/or nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx with NVTX ranges around F/B.
- Extract: per-rank CUDA kernel busy fraction, gaps between consecutive kernels on the compute stream, and NCCL kernel durations. This independently validates (i) the JSONL timeline and (ii) the idle-category attribution. Profiler runs are short (10 active steps) precisely to keep overhead low; they are cross-checks, not the primary metric.

=====================================================================
4) ANALYSIS PLAN
=====================================================================
4.1 Claimed vs measured: for each arm-cell, tabulate:
  scheduler_claimed_bubble_rate (from automatic scheduler output) | bubble_rate_A | bubble_rate_B | 1F1B theoretical.
  Primary comparison: bubble_rate_A and bubble_rate_B for ZB-2p vs the scheduler's claim and vs 1F1B measured in the same cell.
4.2 Near-zero operational threshold (explicit): "near-zero" is defined as measured steady-state bubble rate < 2% by Method A AND < 4% by Method B (B's looser bar because it absorbs comm/launch overhead by construction). Report the verdict per threshold; if the stricter bar fails but the looser passes, report "near-zero under comm-inclusive definition only" rather than a binary yes/no.
4.3 Residual bubble attribution (per-stage idle breakdown): classify each idle interval on each rank into:
  (a) schedule-imposed idle — idle predicted by the schedule structure itself (compare against the automatic scheduler's timeline; gaps present in the scheduler's own plan);
  (b) comm wait — rank ready but blocked on P2P/NCCL (identified via NCCL kernel duration / recv-pending markers, cross-checked with nsys);
  (c) CPU launch gap — no pending work queued, GPU idle, launch thread not ready (torch profiler CPU-side gaps);
  (d) unattributed/other (stragglers, jitter) — reported as remainder.
  Output: stacked per-stage idle breakdown per arm-cell; this tells us WHY ZB-2p misses or hits near-zero, not just whether.
4.4 Statistics: each arm-cell run ≥3 times (fresh processes, interleaved order to decorrelate thermal/clock drift); report mean ± std for bubble_rate_A, bubble_rate_B, throughput, and per-category idle fractions. With n=3, use mean±std descriptively (no inferential test claimed); if the effect size vs 1F1B is within noise, say so.

=====================================================================
5) CONTROLS & VALIDITY THREATS
=====================================================================
- OOM risk (ZB-2p holds up to 2×p pending backward activations): small model + memory logging per rank (max_memory_allocated/reserved per iteration). Pre-check: run 1 warmup-only ZB-2p pass at B2 (p=8) first; if OOM, reduce activation footprint (smaller seq_len) rather than reducing m (which would confound the bubble measurement). Report peak memory per arm — also verifies ZB-2p's memory trade-off claim directionally.
- Clock synchronization / cross-rank jitter: all ranks on one node; synchronize ranks with a barrier + shared reference timestamp before logging; use CLOCK_MONOTONIC per rank with an offset calibration from the barrier. Sensitivity check: recompute bubble_rate_A with a ±1 ms jitter perturbation; if the verdict flips, the answer is "not resolvable at this granularity" — reported as such.
- NCCL warmup effects: ≥20 warmup iterations before any measurement; additionally a comm-only warmup phase so first-touch NCCL costs don't leak into the steady-state window. Verify steady state by checking iteration-time drift <2% across the measured window.
- Measurement-overhead control: JSONL logging is buffered (no per-event flush); profiler runs separate from timing runs; report timing-run overhead estimate (time the logging path itself).
- Confound control: same process count, same CUDA/NCCL versions, pinned clocks if permitted (or report clocks), interleaved arm order, same data shapes (no dynamic shapes).
- Positive control (1F1B vs theory, §2) is the gate for measurement validity.

=====================================================================
6) FEASIBILITY STATEMENT (assumption-labeled)
=====================================================================
- ASSUMPTION: Total budget ~1 hour on ≥4 (ideally 8) GPUs is sufficient: 4 cells × 4 arms × ~50 iterations × ~0.1-0.2 s/iter ≈ minutes of GPU time; the rest is setup, microbenchmarks, and profiler runs. Since resources are unstated, this budget is an assumption, not a fact; the design degrades gracefully (drop cells B1/B2 first, then ARM 4) if the budget is smaller.
- ASSUMPTION: Execution environment provides multi-GPU access + network (current sandbox provides neither). All repo-specific details (flag names, scheduler output format, ZB-V/ZB-H availability) are assumptions to be verified in step 0 before any run.
- Feasibility checks possible before full runs: (i) step-0 source verification; (ii) single-iteration dry run per arm to validate logging; (iii) positive-control check (1F1B vs (p−1)/(m+p−1)) before trusting any ZB-2p number.

=====================================================================
EXPECTED OUTCOME FORMAT (not a result)
=====================================================================
Final report = table of claimed vs measured bubble rates (A and B) per arm-cell, per-stage idle attribution stacks, mean±std over repeats, and an explicit verdict against the stated thresholds — with the answer to the research question remaining an empirical output of running this design, not asserted here.
